stories.title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK
stories.summary: The government is launching the first study to measure PFAS in the UK population to understand the risks. The government is launching its first study into the levels of so-called 'forever chemicals' in the UK population. By taking blood and urine samples, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) hopes to gain a better understanding of any potential health risks caused by the substances also known as PFAS, as well as other potential contaminants like lead and arsenic. It said current evidence suggested the possible health impacts associated with PFAS are likely to be limited, but said the strongest links found in large population groups have been to raised cholesterol and lower birth weights.

stories.title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored
stories.summary: Researchers have detected signals from the smallest distances ever probed. Scientists have picked up signals from the smallest scale of nature ever explored – 100 billion times smaller than an atom. The research, led by scientists based in Cambridge, was obtained from an experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). This vast machine at the European Laboratory for Particle Physics (Cern) on the Swiss-French border smashes atoms together to break them apart and discover what is inside them. The result is important because it could help researchers develop a new, more complete theory of how the Universe works.

stories.summary: Point Of Law ridden by Ethan Brown has won Australia's "race that stops a nation". Australian jockey Ethan Brown has ridden Point Of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles, to victory in this year's Melbourne Cup, the country's most prestigious race. Point of Law, which was bought from the King earlier this year for an undisclosed sum, was considered an early favourite. Brown pushed Point Of Law from the middle of the pack to take the lead with just a few hundred metres to go. The Melbourne Cup has run in Australia since 1861, often referred to as the "race that stops a nation". With a prize of A$10.2m ($7.04m; £5.3m), it is the country's third richest race.
